name: British fascism
summary: British fascism is the family of ultranationalist, authoritarian movements of interwar and later Britain, above all Oswald Mosley's British Union of Fascists. It wanted to replace parliamentary party politics with a strong leader and a corporate state in which employers, workers and finance are organised by industry under state authority, with protection and an economically self-contained nation and Empire. It promised national rebirth, hostility to Communism and alien finance, and opposed immigration and race-mixing, with antisemitism growing in the BUF and central to Leese's Imperial Fascist League.
scope: British fascism as the scholarship on it (Rubin, Burrows, May) describes it: the interwar fascist movements of Britain, above all Oswald Mosley's British Union of Fascists (1932-1940), whose programme The Greater Britain (1932) set out a corporate state with occupational representation under a strong leader, with the Imperial Fascist League of Arnold Leese as the openly racial, Nazi-aligned strand and earlier groups such as the British Fascisti. Postwar groups (Union Movement, National Front, BNP) are heirs, not part of this scope.

no-central-bank.rationale: Mosley criticises the Bank of England as unsuited to industrial reconstruction, but proposes a statutory central-bank monopoly in which Empire gold reserves are pooled.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Duty to the state and discipline are central to Mosley's creed, and he subordinated the individual to the nation.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Mosley praises the Crown as an impartial institution that, as a constitutional Monarch, calls ministers the nation will confirm in a fresh vote.

office-by-exam.rationale: Fascism put authority in the leader and a corporate state with occupational representation, not in examined officials; it also claimed to scorn party patronage.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

open-borders.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

organic-representation.rationale: The occupational franchise: "A steel worker will vote as a steel worker; a doctor as a doctor, a mother as a mother."

parents-choose-intersex-surgery.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The BUF aimed to replace party-political Parliament with an occupationally elected body under a government with wide powers, so Parliament was not to be supreme.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The occupational franchise and leader-led corporate state replaced direct local participation with hierarchical state authority.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mosley says "voluntary discipline is the essence of the Modern Movement" and that Fascist leadership must lead and its discipline be respected.

party-own-road.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

patriotic-education.rationale: The BUF demanded a youth moulded to serve the nation, with national loyalty as the first aim of schooling.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The BUF joined national rebirth with a corporate state serving workers and employers alike, but it did not extend solidarity abroad.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

pay-off-national-debt.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

person-over-state.rationale: The corporate state places everything "within the State; none outside the State; none against the State", and Mosley subordinates liberty to national organisation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

political-borders-follow-ecosystems.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Mosley condemns committee government and wants a Leader who takes absolute responsibility for decisions.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mosley attacked the Parliamentary system and old parties as obstructive, talk-driven and unable to act.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Mosley says the movement does not seek violence and seeks its aims "by methods which are both legal and constitutional", while meeting force with force in defence.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mosley blamed overproduction against weak demand, not population, for unemployment.

population-transfer.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mosley linked unemployment to weak purchasing power and wanted to guarantee economic security, but freedom was framed as duty and obligation.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The BUF sought a single strong leader and a corporate state in place of party politics, which excludes sharing power among rival communities.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mosley says "whatever is good in the past we both respect and venerate", keeping the Crown while rebuilding the instruments of government.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Corporations were to regulate wages and prices by permanent machinery.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

price-stability-first.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The corporate state aimed at national interest, with attention to the unemployed but not poor-first priority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: All within the state; security and justice are state functions.

production-for-use.rationale: Mosley wanted production tied to national consumption and purchasing power but kept enterprise and profit within limits.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mosley allowed enterprise and profit and rejected the Marxist analysis of class war.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Mosley wants to end the "conspiracy" to foist western parliamentary institutions on India just as the West discards them.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property and profit were kept but all within the state and subject to national limits ("none outside the State"), so it is not a near-absolute right.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property and profit were allowed only within national limits and under the state.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based parliamentary representation was rejected in favour of an occupational franchise.

public-money-creation.rationale: Mosley's plan subordinated finance to the state and proposed state control of credit, though he did not demand abolition of bank lending.

public-ownership.rationale: He rejected Whitehall socialism for the self-government of industry in corporations; industries stayed privately owned under state authority.

public-service-media.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

publish-international-agreements.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

race-social-construct.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

racial-oppression-before-sexism.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

racial-pride.rationale: Mosley says the earth will be developed by the races fitted for the task, "and chief among such races we are not afraid to number our own".

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

recall-officials.rationale: Mosley said voters could still remove governments, but no explicit recall mechanism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: British fascism rejected parliamentary and party democracy in favor of a strong leader, and an instructed recallable delegate system runs against that.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: Mosley bases Britain's right to be in India on "the power of original conquest", as with earlier conquerors, used for construction rather than oppression.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

refuse-to-join-illegitimate-government.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Industry and finance were to sit under state authority, with finance made the handmaid of industry, which means tighter regulation.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

religious-nation.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

residents-only-property.rationale: The corporate state was centralised under national authority, so local bodies limiting property purchases would cut across it.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mosley says Fascism is not reaction: stability needs progress and progress needs stability, with a revolution in methods of government.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: State authority and obligation in public life were justified by national economic renewal.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were to be replaced by corporate arbitration of wages, though secret ballots were not the method.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mosley stressed action over committees and talk but also a defined ideology of the corporate state.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

revive-national-language.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National-first autarky with no foreign obligations.

rich-first.rationale: The corporate state emphasised national solidarity and planned industry, opposing letting some groups get rich first.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

rule-by-example.rationale: The leader and disciplined youth were to inspire by dedication, but laws and force were also used.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Mosley held that the old parties served finance and were to be replaced by authority and dynamism; consent-through-culture is not his framing.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture was to be saved by protection and exclusion of foreign food, and fascist rhetoric valued the countryside, but the BUF was an industrial modernist movement.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fascism promised national rebirth and treated the nation as an organic whole above individuals; The Greater Britain makes service to the nation the highest duty.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

say-in-proportion-to-effect.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

self-interest-moral.rationale: "Liberty in private life. Obligation in public life." The doctrine put national duty above self-interest.

self-ownership.rationale: Mosley's corporate state subordinated the individual to national duty and service, rejecting liberal individualism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autarchy, the self-contained Nation and Empire, was a stated aim of the BUF.

separate-church-state.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

separated-powers.rationale: Mosley wanted strong executive government and denounced Parliament's obstruction.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatism denies conflicting class interests and subordinates all to a national good set by the state.

slavery-reparations.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: The Greater Britain venerates the Crown and what is good in the past, yet wants the remaining instruments of government "drastically altered" and the House of Lords replaced.

social-market-economy.rationale: The corporate state aimed at state-organised cooperation of capital and labour, not social-market or laissez-faire models; split.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Autarky of nation and Empire is the aim, and Marxist internationalism is rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: The question presupposes socialist ownership; the BUF rejected socialism but did envisage markets within corporate limits, so mild disagreement.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state stands above classes and is the arbiter of all.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mosley wanted British finance directed to equip British industry and the state to guide rationalised industry.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

state-harmful.rationale: The corporate state placed everything "within the State; none outside the State; none against the State."

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Concerns the Soviet case; no relevant position for British fascism.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

strong-leader.rationale: Mosley wanted strong executive government and equated Dictatorship with Leadership, bypassing a Parliament of obstruction and talk.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The BUF aimed to replace party politics with a single leader and corporate state and used the Public Order Act context to attack rivals.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protection was central, though conditional on wages and prices: "Protection must protect organisation, and not chaos."

tax-holding-cash.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mosley saw rationalised industry as inevitable and thought the rationalised state could master its effects, a technocratic modernism.

technology-design-reflects-political-int.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

total-state.rationale: "All within the State; none outside the State; none against the State."

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The BUF opposed Communism and presented fascism as a legitimate order, so it rejected the equivalence.

trade-surplus.rationale: Exports were a surplus after the large home market was served.

traditional-family.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Fascist rebirth rhetoric presents Britain's greatness as continuous from a heroic past into a revived Greater Britain.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were to be folded into the state's corporate machinery and denied independent class-struggle roles, so independent unions are not praised.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Mosley weaves unions and employers into corporations that work "under the general guidance of corporative government", with wages settled by State arbitration.

universal-morality.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A leader unconstrained by Parliament would hold power until removed, though Mosley said voters could remove governments.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: Mosley calls motherhood one of the highest callings and the wife and mother a main pillar of the State, not an exploited condition.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

voluntary-union-payments-at-work.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mosley defended agriculture and enterprise but also rationalised large industry; no clear small-owner programme in the sources opened.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Fascism demanded active service, action and national rebirth, the opposite of withdrawal.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nulled: the saved sources (Mosley's The Greater Britain, Rubin, Burrows, May) do not state a position on this statement; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and the later National Front.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: The Greater Britain proposes organising and representing mothers as such through their own corporate body, apart from the men's corporations.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejected socialism; workers and employers were to cooperate in state-supervised corporations, not workers owning firms.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

workers-councils.rationale: Corporations under state authority replaced parliaments, but as state bodies and not councils of workers holding power.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers were integrated into the national corporate state, not an international class.

workers-own-party.rationale: The BUF replaced class parties with the corporate state and attacked Communism and all party politics, so an independent workers' party was rejected.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporations were state-supervised bodies, not democratic votes of workers and public.

youth-equal-civil-rights.rationale: The saved sources record no position on this statement.

missingStatements.text: Parliament should be replaced by a body elected by occupation rather than by geographic constituency.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley's occupational franchise, where a steel worker votes as a steel worker and a mother as a mother, was central to the corporate state.

missingStatements.text: A country and its colonies should form a self-sufficient economic bloc shut off from outside trade.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley's stated aim was autarchy, the self-contained Nation and Empire, with conditional protection and exclusion of foreign food.

missingStatements.text: Finance should be subordinated to productive industry and national purposes.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosley called finance the handmaid of industry and aimed to direct British finance to equip British industry, attacking alien finance.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to interwar corporatist economics; the positions on regulating corporations and finance are already carried by regulate-corporations, ban-interest and corporatist-bargaining.

missingStatements.text: In peacetime a country should avoid wars unless its own territory or empire is under attack.
missingStatements.rationale: The BUF practised selective pacifism, opposing wars except in defence of Britain or the Empire, and opposed the guarantee to Poland.
missingStatements.declined: Covered loosely by military-superiority, force-without-un and war-builds-character; a conditional pacifism too specific to the BUF to add.

notes: The Mosley BUF mainstream was in its own terms cultural and imperial rather than biologically racial, rejected Nazi racial laws and supported loyalty to the Crown; Leese's Imperial Fascist League and the later National Front were openly racial, antisemitic and pro-Nazi, and would answer race, antisemitism, eugenics and repatriation statements more strongly. Mosley's women's policies (equal pay, ending the marriage bar) coexisted with distinct gender roles. Several answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences.
